# New England-Style Seaside Clambake Menu

Because of your shellfish allergy, this menu replaces the traditional clams, lobster, and mussels with fish, poultry, and vegetables. Every dish is seasoned without added salt, so the menu also suits a low sodium diet. Ask your cook to use separate pots, utensils, and cooking surfaces, since shellfish cross-contact is a real risk at a traditional clambake.

## Starters

Serve a chilled cucumber and dill salad dressed with lemon juice, olive oil, and fresh herbs. Set out a platter of sliced watermelon, peaches, and blueberries for a bright, refreshing start. Warm cornbread made without added salt can also be offered alongside the starters.

## Main Course

Wrap cod fillets in parchment with lemon slices, garlic, and fresh thyme, then steam them over the fire pit until flaky. Roast herb chicken thighs seasoned with paprika, black pepper, garlic powder, and dried oregano. Grill low sodium chicken sausage links, and check the label to confirm the sodium content before you buy them.

## Sides

Cook corn on the cob in its husk, then serve it with herb butter made from unsalted butter. Toss new potatoes with olive oil, chopped parsley, and black pepper, and wrap them in foil so they steam in the pit. Roast sweet potato wedges with cinnamon and a little olive oil until they caramelize. Prepare a crisp coleslaw dressed with apple cider vinegar, a touch of honey, and celery seed. Finish with a green salad of mixed lettuces, cherry tomatoes, and red onion tossed in a light vinaigrette.

## Dessert

Bake a blueberry cobbler with a lightly sweetened topping and serve it warm with vanilla yogurt. Offer a tray of oatmeal cookies made with unsalted butter for guests who want something smaller.

## Beverages

Provide homemade lemonade, unsweetened iced tea, and sparkling water with lime wedges. Keep everything chilled in a cooler near the serving table so guests can refill throughout the afternoon.

# Chicken and Andouille Gumbo (Low Sodium, Shellfish Free)

This gumbo keeps the deep, smoky character of the classic dish without any shellfish. Chicken thighs and andouille sausage provide the protein, and a dark roux gives the body and colour that define the style. Check the andouille label to confirm it contains no shellfish and to find a low sodium option, and use salt-free Cajun seasoning so the dish stays within a low sodium diet.

**Ingredients (serves six)**

- 120 millilitres vegetable oil
- 120 grams plain flour
- 8 bone-in chicken thighs, skin removed
- 300 grams low sodium andouille sausage, sliced
- 1 large onion, diced
- 1 green pepper, diced
- 3 celery stalks, diced
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 1.5 litres low sodium chicken stock
- 1 bay leaf
- 2 teaspoons salt-free Cajun seasoning
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 2 tablespoons chopped flat-leaf parsley
- 4 spring onions, sliced
- Hot sauce, to taste (check for low sodium)
- Cooked long-grain white rice, to serve

**Method**

Heat the oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and whisk in the flour. Keep whisking for 25 to 35 minutes until the roux turns a deep chocolate brown. If the roux scorches, discard it and start again, because a burnt roux will spoil the whole pot.

Add the onion, green pepper and celery to the roux and cook for about 5 minutes until the vegetables soften. Add the garlic and cook for one minute more. Pour in the stock a little at a time while whisking to prevent lumps from forming.

Add the chicken, sausage, bay leaf, Cajun seasoning, thyme and paprika to the pot. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to a gentle simmer for 90 minutes, skimming any fat from the surface as it rises. Remove the chicken, shred the meat from the bones and return it to the pot. Simmer for a further 15 minutes, then remove the bay leaf and stir in the parsley, spring onions and hot sauce. Serve the gumbo over rice.

**Side Dish 1: Braised Collard Greens**

Sauté one finely chopped onion and two minced garlic cloves in a tablespoon of olive oil until soft. Add 600 grams of chopped collard greens, 250 millilitres of low sodium vegetable stock, a splash of apple cider vinegar, a pinch of black pepper and a pinch of smoked paprika. Cover the pan and simmer for 30 minutes until the greens are tender.

**Side Dish 2: Cucumber and Tomato Salad**

Combine two diced cucumbers, 250 grams of halved cherry tomatoes and half a thinly sliced red onion in a bowl. Dress the salad with two tablespoons of olive oil, one tablespoon of red wine vinegar, a teaspoon of chopped fresh dill and a pinch of black pepper. Let the salad rest for 10 minutes so the flavours blend before serving.

# Chicken and Andouille Gumbo

**Ingredients (serves four)**

- 1 tablespoon vegetable oil
- 2 tablespoons plain flour
- 1 onion, diced
- 1 green pepper, diced
- 2 celery sticks, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 500 g skinless chicken thighs, cut into chunks
- 150 g andouille sausage, sliced (choose a low sodium version or check the label)
- 1.5 litres low sodium chicken stock
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon cayenne pepper, adjusted to taste
- 2 spring onions, sliced, to garnish
- A handful of fresh parsley, chopped, to garnish

**Method**

Heat the oil in a large, heavy pot over medium heat. Add the flour and stir constantly for about 15 minutes, until the roux turns a deep brown, about the colour of milk chocolate. Take care not to let it burn.

Add the onion, pepper and celery to the pot. Cook for 8 minutes, until soft. Stir in the garlic and cook for one minute more.

Add the chicken and sausage and cook for 5 minutes. Pour in the stock, then add the bay leaf, thyme, paprika and cayenne. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 45 minutes, skimming off any foam that rises to the surface.

Remove the bay leaf. Season with black pepper and a squeeze of lemon juice instead of salt. Serve in deep bowls over rice, topped with spring onions and parsley.

# Two Sides

**1. Low Sodium Cornbread**

- 150 g cornmeal
- 150 g plain flour
- 1 tablespoon baking powder
- 1 tablespoon sugar
- 1 egg
- 240 ml milk
- 60 ml vegetable oil

Heat the oven to 200°C and grease a 20 cm square tin. Mix the dry ingredients in one bowl and the wet ingredients in another. Combine the two, then pour the batter into the tin. Bake for 20 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.

**2. Collard Greens Without Ham Hock**

- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 onion, sliced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 500 g collard greens, stems removed and leaves chopped
- 120 ml low sodium vegetable stock
- 1 tablespoon cider vinegar
- Black pepper and a squeeze of lemon juice to finish

Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for one minute. Add the greens and stock, then cover and cook for 20 minutes, until tender. Stir in the vinegar and finish with pepper and lemon juice.

**Chicken and Smoked Turkey Gumbo**

Serves six. This version uses no shellfish and no added salt, so it suits a shellfish allergy and a low sodium diet. Check that your Cajun seasoning and stock labels confirm they contain no shellfish.

**Ingredients**

- 60 g plain flour
- 60 ml vegetable oil
- 1 onion, chopped small
- 1 green pepper, chopped small
- 2 celery sticks, chopped small
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon cayenne pepper
- 1 teaspoon salt-free Cajun seasoning
- 1.5 litres low sodium chicken stock
- 500 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
- 200 g smoked turkey breast, diced (choose a low sodium variety if you can find one)
- 1 can (400 g) chopped tomatoes with no added salt
- 250 g okra, sliced
- 2 spring onions, sliced
- 2 tablespoons chopped parsley
- Cooked long-grain rice, to serve

**Method**

Toss the chicken with the Cajun seasoning and set it aside. Whisk the flour and oil together in a heavy pot over medium heat, then stir without stopping for 20 to 25 minutes until the roux turns a deep chocolate brown. A burnt roux tastes bitter, so discard it and begin again if it turns black.

Add the onion, green pepper and celery to the roux and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic, thyme, paprika, cayenne and bay leaves, and cook for one minute more.

Pour in the stock a little at a time, stirring as you go, then add the chicken, turkey and tomatoes. Bring the pot to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 45 minutes, skimming any foam from the surface. Add the okra and simmer for a further 15 minutes until tender. Remove the bay leaves, stir in the spring onions and parsley, and serve over rice.

**Two Sides**

**Braised collard greens:** Remove the stems from 500 g of collard greens and slice the leaves into strips. Cook a chopped onion and two garlic cloves in a splash of oil for 3 minutes, then add the greens, 250 ml of no-salt-added stock and a tablespoon of cider vinegar. Cover and cook for 30 to 40 minutes until the greens are soft, then finish with black pepper and a pinch of cayenne. The vinegar cuts through the richness of the gumbo.

**Skillet cornbread:** Combine 150 g cornmeal, 100 g plain flour, 2 teaspoons low sodium baking powder, 1 tablespoon sugar, 240 ml milk, 2 beaten eggs and 60 ml melted butter. Pour the batter into a hot, greased 25 cm cast iron skillet and bake at 200°C for 20 to 25 minutes until golden at the edges. Cut it into wedges and serve it alongside the gumbo to soak up the broth.

Here are some must-try Indonesian street foods:

- **Nasi goreng**: Fried rice with sweet soy sauce (kecap manis), shallots, garlic, and chili, often topped with a fried egg.
- **Mie goreng**: The noodle version of nasi goreng, usually with vegetables and egg.
- **Sate (satay)**: Skewered and grilled meat, usually chicken (sate ayam) or goat (sate kambing), often served with a sweet soy glaze or peanut sauce.
- **Bakso**: Meatball soup with noodles, rice vermicelli, and fried shallots.
- **Soto ayam**: Turmeric-yellow chicken soup with glass noodles, boiled egg, and lime.
- **Bubur ayam**: Chicken rice porridge topped with shredded chicken, crispy fried shallots, and soy sauce.
- **Martabak**: A thick pancake, either sweet (with chocolate, cheese, or banana) or savory (stuffed with egg, meat, and scallions).
- **Pempek**: Palembang fish cakes served with a tangy, sweet-sour sauce called cuko.
- **Es cendol**: A chilled dessert of green rice-flour jelly, coconut milk, and palm sugar syrup.

**Peanut warning:** Gado-gado, siomay, batagor, and most satay sauces are made with peanut sauce (saus kacang). "Kacang" means peanut, so check any dish with a sauce before ordering. Vendors often use shared woks and utensils, so cross-contamination is possible even in dishes that seem peanut-free. Ask for the dish without peanut sauce, and show the vendor this phrase: "Saya alergi kacang" (I'm allergic to peanuts). Sate ayam served with kecap manis (sweet soy sauce) instead of peanut sauce is a safer choice, as are nasi goreng, soto ayam, and es cendol, though you should still confirm no peanuts are added.

# West African Dinner for Six

## Menu
- **Main:** Nigerian-style beef stew with ginger, garlic and scotch bonnet
- **Side 1:** Jollof rice
- **Side 2:** Fried ripe plantains
- **Garnish:** Fresh parsley, scattered over the stew and rice

## Beef Stew (serves 6)
**Ingredients**
- 1.2 kg beef chuck, cut into bite-sized cubes
- 3 tbsp vegetable oil
- 2 onions, one finely chopped and one blended
- 4 garlic cloves, crushed
- A thumb-sized piece of ginger, grated
- 1 kg ripe tomatoes, blended (or 400 g tinned tomatoes, drained)
- 2 red peppers, blended
- 1 to 2 scotch bonnets, to taste
- 2 tbsp tomato purée
- 1 litre unsalted or low-sodium beef stock
- 2 tsp dried thyme, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp smoked paprika, ½ tsp black pepper

**Method**
1. Season the beef with pepper and a little paprika. Brown it in 2 tbsp oil in batches, then set aside.
2. Fry the chopped onion, garlic and ginger in the remaining oil until soft.
3. Add the blended onion, tomatoes, peppers and scotch bonnet. Simmer for 20 minutes until the oil separates and the sauce thickens.
4. Stir in the tomato purée, then return the beef with the stock, thyme and bay leaves.
5. Cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours until the beef is tender, adding a splash of water if it thickens too quickly.

## Jollof Rice (serves 6)
**Ingredients**
- 500 g parboiled long grain rice (a large sack from your grocer keeps costs down)
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 onion, chopped, and 1 red pepper, chopped
- 600 g ripe tomatoes, blended
- 1 tbsp tomato purée
- 600 ml low-sodium stock
- 1 tsp dried thyme, 1 bay leaf, 1 tsp curry powder, half a scotch bonnet

**Method**
1. Fry the onion and pepper in the oil until soft, then add the tomato purée and cook for 2 minutes.
2. Add the blended tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes until reduced.
3. Stir in the spices, then add the rinsed rice and stock. Bring to a simmer.
4. Cover tightly and cook on low for 25 minutes. Rest, covered, for 10 minutes before fluffing.

## Fried Plantains (serves 6)
- 3 very ripe plantains, skin mostly black
- Vegetable oil for shallow frying

Peel and slice the plantains diagonally into 1 cm pieces. Fry in hot oil for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden at the edges. Drain on kitchen paper. Plantains are naturally low in sodium, so they need no added salt.

## Dietary Notes
- **Peanut-free:** Avoid suya spice and groundnut oil, and check the label on any curry powder for peanut traces.
- **Low sodium:** Skip stock cubes, which are high in salt. Homemade or low-sodium stock works well, and the aromatics provide plenty of flavour.
- **Herbs:** Parsley replaces cilantro in the garnish.

## Timeline
- **Morning:** Blend the tomatoes, onions and peppers for both dishes. Cut the beef and plantains.
- **Two and a half hours before serving:** Start the stew.
- **Forty-five minutes before serving:** Start the jollof.
- **Fifteen minutes before serving:** Fry the plantains just before the table is set so they stay warm and crisp.

# West African Dinner for Six

## Menu
- **Main stew:** Beef and egusi (melon seed) stew with spinach
- **Side 1:** Smoky jollof rice
- **Side 2:** Kelewele (spiced fried plantain)

## Allergy and Dietary Notes
- **Peanuts:** Groundnut stew is a common West African dish, but this menu avoids it. Check that the oil is not groundnut oil, since many kitchens use it for frying. Use palm oil or vegetable oil.
- **Low sodium:** Skip stock cubes, which are very high in salt. Use unsalted stock and season with ginger, garlic, thyme and smoked paprika. Use only a small amount of ground crayfish, or leave it out.
- **Cilantro:** Use flat-leaf parsley wherever a recipe calls for coriander.
- **Eggplant:** Not used in this menu.

## Shopping List
- 1 kg beef chuck, cut into chunks
- 200 g ground egusi (melon seeds)
- 200 ml palm oil, plus extra for frying
- 1 bunch fresh spinach, or bitter leaf if available
- 1 kg long-grain rice (buying a large sack is cost-effective)
- 4 ripe plantains
- 1 large onion, 3 garlic cloves, 1 thumb of ginger
- 4 ripe tomatoes and 2 red bell peppers
- 1 to 2 scotch bonnet chillies (adjust to heat preference)
- Fresh thyme, smoked paprika, ground black pepper
- Unsalted beef stock, 1 litre
- Flat-leaf parsley

## Timeline

**Day before:** Marinate the beef in garlic, ginger, thyme and pepper. Refrigerate overnight.

**Two to three hours before:** Simmer the beef in stock until tender, about 1.5 to 2 hours.

**One hour before:** Start the jollof rice and prepare the plantains.

**Thirty minutes before:** Finish the egusi stew and fry the kelewele just before serving.

## Recipes

### 1. Beef and Egusi Stew
1. Brown the beef in a little palm oil, then remove and set aside.
2. Blend the onion, tomatoes, peppers and scotch bonnet into a smooth paste.
3. Fry the paste in 100 ml of palm oil for about 10 minutes, until the oil rises to the surface.
4. Mix the ground egusi with a splash of water to form a loose paste, then stir it into the pot. Fry for 5 minutes, stirring constantly so it does not clump.
5. Add the beef and about 500 ml of the simmering stock. Simmer for 20 minutes.
6. Stir in the shredded spinach and cook for 3 to 5 minutes until wilted.
7. Taste and adjust with pepper and herbs. Add salt only if needed, and keep it light.

### 2. Smoky Jollof Rice
1. Blend 2 tomatoes, 1 red pepper, 1 scotch bonnet and half an onion.
2. Fry the rest of the onion in palm oil until golden, then add the blended mixture and cook down for 15 minutes.
3. Add 2 teaspoons of smoked paprika, thyme and pepper.
4. Stir in 2 cups of rinsed rice and 3 cups of unsalted stock. Cover and cook on low for 25 to 30 minutes.
5. Rest for 10 minutes before serving, so the grains firm up.

### 3. Kelewele
1. Cut the plantains into cubes and set aside.
2. Blend 1 scotch bonnet, grated ginger, 1 garlic clove, a pinch of ground pepper and a little smoked paprika into a paste.
3. Toss the plantain cubes in the paste and leave for 15 minutes.
4. Fry in hot vegetable oil until golden and slightly caramelised on the edges, about 3 to 4 minutes.
5. Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

## Serving
Serve the egusi stew in a wide bowl, with jollof rice and kelewele on the side. Garnish with chopped parsley and a few thin slices of scotch bonnet for those who want extra heat.

# West African Dinner for Six

**Menu:** Nigerian-style beef stew, jollof rice, and kelewele (spiced fried plantains)

**Allergy and dietary notes:**
- **Peanut allergy:** Avoid groundnut stew and groundnut oil. Many spice blends, including suya spice, contain ground peanut, so check labels or make your own spice mix. Use sunflower or vegetable oil.
- **Cilantro:** Use flat-leaf parsley or spring onion for garnish.
- **Low sodium:** Use unsalted or low-sodium stock. Bouillon cubes such as Maggi are very high in sodium, so skip them. Season mainly with scotch bonnet, ginger, garlic, thyme, and bay, and add salt sparingly at the end.
- **Eggplant:** Not included.

## Shopping List

- 1.2 kg beef chuck, cut into 3 cm cubes
- 2 kg ripe plum tomatoes (about 12) or 1 large can unsalted chopped tomatoes
- 2 large red bell peppers
- 2 to 3 scotch bonnet peppers (adjust to heat tolerance)
- 4 large onions
- 1 head garlic
- 1 thumb-sized piece fresh ginger
- 3 tbsp tomato purée
- 500 g long-grain parboiled rice (a large sack is economical if you cook often)
- 1.5 litres low-sodium beef stock
- 4 ripe plantains (yellow with black spots)
- Dried thyme, bay leaves, curry powder (check the label for peanuts), ground ginger, cayenne pepper
- Fresh parsley and spring onions for garnish
- Sunflower or vegetable oil

## Beef Stew

1. Season the beef with a little black pepper and a teaspoon of thyme. Brown in batches in 2 tbsp oil until deeply coloured, then set aside.
2. Blend 6 tomatoes, 2 peppers, 1 scotch bonnet, 1 onion, and the garlic and ginger until smooth.
3. In the same pot, fry 2 finely sliced onions in 3 tbsp oil until soft. Add the tomato purée and fry for 2 minutes until it darkens.
4. Pour in the blended mixture and simmer for 15 minutes until the oil rises to the surface.
5. Return the beef, add the stock, 2 bay leaves, and 1 tsp curry powder. Simmer covered on low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until tender.
6. Taste and add a small pinch of salt only if needed.

## Jollof Rice

1. Blend 6 tomatoes, 1 red pepper, 1 scotch bonnet, and 1 onion until smooth.
2. Heat 4 tbsp oil in a wide pot. Fry the remaining onion until soft, then add 2 tbsp tomato purée and fry until dark.
3. Pour in the blended tomato mixture and simmer for 15 minutes.
4. Stir in 1 tsp thyme, 1 tsp curry powder, and 2 bay leaves.
5. Rinse the rice, add it to the pot, and stir to coat. Pour in 600 ml low-sodium stock, enough to just cover the rice.
6. Cover tightly and cook on low for 25 to 30 minutes until the rice is tender and the bottom is slightly toasted. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

## Kelewele

1. Peel the plantains and cut them into 1 cm cubes.
2. Mix with 1 tsp ground ginger, 1/2 tsp cayenne, 1 finely grated garlic clove, and 1 finely chopped scotch bonnet.
3. Leave to marinate for 15 minutes.
4. Shallow-fry in hot oil for 3 to 4 minutes per side until edges are caramelised.
5. Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

## Timing Plan

- **Morning:** Shop and check all labels for peanut-containing ingredients.
- **3 hours before:** Start the beef stew.
- **1 hour before:** Prepare the jollof base and marinate the plantains.
- **30 minutes before:** Cook the rice and fry the kelewele just before serving.
- **At serving:** Garnish the stew with parsley and spring onion, and serve everything together.

# West African Dinner for Six

- **Side two:** Fried plantains (dodo)

Egusi is made from ground melon seeds, so it contains no peanuts. Check every packaged ingredient and spice blend for peanut traces, and ask your butcher and grocer about cross-contact.

## Egusi Stew with Beef and Spinach

**Ingredients (serves six):**
- 1.2 kg beef chuck, cut into chunks
- 1 cup ground egusi (melon seed)
- 500 ml palm oil or vegetable oil
- 2 large onions, one blended and one finely chopped
- 3 ripe tomatoes and 2 red peppers, blended
- 2 scotch bonnet peppers, blended (adjust to taste)
- 1 tablespoon crayfish powder (optional)
- 2 beef stock cubes, checked for peanut-free labelling
- 500 g fresh spinach or bitter leaf, washed and chopped
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1 litre water

**Method:**
1. Season the beef with salt, one stock cube, and half the chopped onion. Simmer in water for about 45 minutes until tender, then strain and keep the stock.
2. Heat the oil in a large pot and fry the remaining chopped onion until golden.
3. Add the blended tomato, pepper, and scotch bonnet mixture. Fry for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until the oil rises to the surface.
4. Mix the egusi with a little cold water to form a thick paste, then drop small spoonfuls into the pot. Stir gently and fry for 5 minutes so the seeds clump into soft lumps.
5. Add the beef, stock, and crayfish. Simmer for 20 minutes.
6. Stir in the spinach and cook for 5 more minutes. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

Garnish with chopped spring onion or parsley instead of cilantro.

## Jollof Rice

**Ingredients (serves six):**
- 3 cups long-grain parboiled rice
- 4 ripe tomatoes and 2 red peppers, blended
- 1 onion, chopped
- 3 tablespoons tomato paste
- 80 ml vegetable oil
- 2 scotch bonnet peppers, blended
- 2 bay leaves, 1 teaspoon thyme, and 1 teaspoon curry powder
- 2 stock cubes
- 4 cups stock or water

**Method:**
1. Fry the onion in the oil until soft, then add the tomato paste and fry for 3 minutes.
2. Add the blended tomato and pepper mixture and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until the oil separates.
3. Stir in the seasonings and stock cubes, then add the stock or water and bring to a boil.
4. Rinse the rice, add it to the pot, cover, and cook on low heat for 25 minutes without stirring.
5. Fluff gently with a fork. For a smoky finish, cover the pot with foil for the last 10 minutes on low heat.

For a dinner of six, buying rice in a large sack from a grocer will keep costs down.

## Fried Plantains (Dodo)

**Ingredients:**
- 3 ripe plantains (yellow with black spots)
- Vegetable oil for frying
- A pinch of salt
- Optional: a little cayenne pepper

**Method:**
1. Peel the plantains and slice them diagonally into rounds about 1 cm thick.
2. Heat about 1 cm of oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
3. Fry the slices for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden at the edges.
4. Drain on kitchen paper and sprinkle with salt and cayenne.

Serve the dodo while warm.

## Timeline

- **Two days ahead:** Buy ingredients and check labels for peanut traces.
- **Morning:** Cook the beef stock and prepare the blended sauce base for the jollof and stew.
- **Two hours before serving:** Start the egusi stew, which tastes better when it rests.
- **One hour before serving:** Cook the jollof rice.
- **Just before serving:** Fry the plantains and reheat the stew gently.

## Menu Overview

This dinner centres on a Nigerian beef stew with a rich tomato and pepper base. It serves six generously and comes with two sides: jollof rice and fried plantain. Most of the work can happen the day before, which leaves you free on the night.

## Allergy and Ingredient Notes

This menu contains no groundnuts or peanut oil, but check labels on stock cubes, seasoning blends and cooking oils for peanut content. Keep all peanut products out of the kitchen to prevent cross-contact. Parsley replaces coriander in every recipe.

## Main Course: Beef and Pepper Stew

**Ingredients for six**

- One and a half kilograms beef chuck, cut into cubes
- Two onions, one roughly chopped and one thinly sliced
- Six ripe plum tomatoes
- Three red bell peppers
- Two scotch bonnet chillies, deseeded if you prefer less heat
- Two tablespoons tomato purée
- Four tablespoons sunflower or vegetable oil
- Two stock cubes, confirmed peanut-free
- Two bay leaves
- One teaspoon dried thyme
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Two tablespoons chopped fresh parsley

**Method**

Season the beef with salt, pepper and half a crumbled stock cube. Place it in a large pot with the chopped onion, one bay leaf and enough water to cover, then simmer for about ninety minutes until tender. Keep the stock.

Blend the tomatoes, peppers, chillies and the purée into a smooth paste. Heat the oil in a wide pan, fry the sliced onion until golden, then add the paste and cook for twenty to thirty minutes, stirring often, until the oil rises to the surface and the sauce darkens.

Add the beef, a ladle or two of its stock, the remaining stock cube, the second bay leaf and the thyme. Simmer for twenty minutes, then stir in the parsley and adjust the seasoning. The stew tastes even better after resting overnight.

## Side One: Jollof Rice

**Ingredients for six**

- Three cups parboiled long-grain rice
- Four tomatoes and one red pepper, blended
- One onion, finely chopped
- Three tablespoons vegetable oil
- Two teaspoons curry powder
- One teaspoon thyme
- Two bay leaves
- Two stock cubes dissolved in about four cups of hot water

**Method**

Fry the onion in the oil until soft, then add the blended tomato and pepper. Cook this down for about fifteen minutes, until the oil separates. Stir in the curry powder, thyme and bay leaves.

Add the rice and stir to coat, then pour in the stock until the rice is just covered. Cover tightly and cook on low heat for about thirty-five minutes, checking once or twice and adding a splash of water if it looks dry. Rest the pot covered for ten minutes before serving.

Buying rice in a large sack from a grocer costs less per portion and suits a dinner for a group.

## Side Two: Fried Plantain

**Ingredients for six**

- Four ripe plantains, the skins mostly black
- Vegetable oil for frying
- A pinch of salt

**Method**

Peel the plantains and slice them diagonally into pieces about one centimetre thick. Heat about two centimetres of oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the slices for three to four minutes per side until deep golden and caramelised at the edges. Drain on kitchen paper, sprinkle with salt, and serve while warm.

## Timing Plan

**The day before:** Make the stew, cool it quickly, then refrigerate. Prepare the jollof base and keep it covered in the fridge.

**Morning of the dinner:** Slice the plantains and keep them in cold water until needed.

**About an hour before guests arrive:** Reheat the stew gently over low heat, stirring occasionally. Cook the jollof rice, then keep it covered to stay warm.

**Just before serving:** Fry the plantains so they arrive hot and crisp.

# West African Dinner for Six

The menu centres on egusi stew, a hearty Nigerian dish thickened with ground melon seeds and leafy greens. It pairs with jollof rice and fried plantains, which give the table a good balance of smoky, sweet and savoury flavours.

**Allergy note:** Many West African dishes use groundnuts (peanuts), including maafe and some suya spice blends. This menu contains none of them, but check the labels on stock cubes, spice mixes and oils before you cook, and confirm with your guests about any other allergies.

## Egusi Stew (serves six)

Ingredients:
- two cups ground egusi (melon seeds)
- one kilogram beef or goat, cut into chunks
- two onions, one blended and one finely chopped
- three tomatoes, blended
- four tablespoons palm oil
- one scotch bonnet pepper, blended
- two cubes beef stock (check the label for peanut traces)
- one bunch spinach or bitter leaf, chopped
- salt and crayfish powder to taste

Method:
Boil the meat with the chopped onion, a stock cube and some salt until tender, which takes about one hour. Save the stock. Heat the palm oil in a large pot, fry the blended onion for a few minutes, then add the blended tomato and pepper and let it reduce until thick. Stir in the ground egusi with a ladle of stock to form a thick paste, then add the meat and enough stock to cover. Simmer gently for twenty to twenty-five minutes, then fold in the spinach and cook for five minutes more.

## Jollof Rice (serves six)

Ingredients:
- three cups long-grain parboiled rice
- four ripe tomatoes and one red pepper, blended
- two onions, chopped
- two tablespoons tomato paste
- one scotch bonnet pepper
- two teaspoons curry powder and one teaspoon dried thyme
- three cups stock
- vegetable oil and salt

Method:
Fry the tomato paste in oil until it darkens, then add the onion and blended tomato and pepper. Simmer until the liquid evaporates and the oil rises to the surface. Add the spices, stock and rinsed rice, cover tightly and cook on low heat for about thirty minutes until the grains are tender. Let the rice rest for ten minutes before serving.

## Fried Plantains (serves six)

Choose plantains that are mostly black and soft, as they will be sweet and caramelised. Peel and slice them on the diagonal into pieces about one centimetre thick. Fry them in hot vegetable oil for three to four minutes per side until golden, then drain on kitchen paper and sprinkle lightly with salt.

## Garnish

Chop a handful of parsley and scatter it over the stew and rice. Parsley works well here and suits anyone who finds coriander unpleasant.

## Timing and Shopping

Start the stew first, as it takes about ninety minutes in total. Begin the jollof rice about forty-five minutes before serving, then fry the plantains just before the meal so they stay warm and crisp. For the rice, buying a large sack from a grocer costs far less per kilogram than small packs, and it lasts through several dinners.

# Spanish Paella Night Menu

## Tapas to Start

- **Patatas bravas:** Crispy roasted potato cubes with a homemade tomato sauce and a light garlic aioli. Use fresh tomatoes and little added salt to keep it low sodium.
- **Pimientos de padrón:** Blistered green peppers in olive oil, finished with a light sprinkle of sea salt.
- **Tortilla española:** A classic potato and onion omelette, served in small wedges.
- **Piquillo peppers stuffed with goat's cheese:** Roasted red peppers filled with fresh, mild goat's cheese, which is naturally lower in sodium than aged cheeses such as Manchego.
- **Pan con tomate:** Toasted sourdough rubbed with ripe tomato, garlic and olive oil.
- **Marinated mushrooms:** Button mushrooms sautéed in olive oil, garlic, sherry vinegar and fresh parsley.

## Main Course: Chicken and Vegetable Paella

*Serves 6*

**Ingredients:**
- 400g paella rice (bomba or Calasparra)
- 500g boneless chicken thighs, cut into pieces
- 1 red pepper and 1 green pepper, sliced
- 150g green beans, trimmed
- 1 onion and 4 garlic cloves, finely chopped
- 2 ripe tomatoes, grated
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika and a generous pinch of saffron threads
- 1.2 litres low-sodium chicken stock, warmed
- 150g fresh or frozen peas
- 60ml olive oil
- Lemon wedges and fresh parsley to garnish

**Method:**
1. Warm the saffron in a few spoonfuls of the hot stock.
2. Season the chicken lightly with pepper and brown it in olive oil in a large paella pan. Remove and set aside.
3. Fry the onion, peppers and green beans until soft, then add the garlic and grated tomato and cook until jammy.
4. Stir in the paprika, rice and saffron stock, then add the remaining stock and return the chicken to the pan.
5. Cook over a medium heat for about 18 minutes without stirring, adding the peas for the final 5 minutes.
6. Rest the paella for 5 minutes, covered loosely with a clean tea towel, then serve with lemon wedges and parsley.

*Note: Traditional paella often includes seafood and chorizo. This version avoids shellfish entirely and skips chorizo to keep the sodium content low.*

## Salad on the Side

- **Ensalada de tomate:** Sliced ripe tomatoes, red onion, olive oil, sherry vinegar and fresh oregano, with no added salt.

## Dessert

- **Crema catalana:** A custard with a caramelised sugar top, flavoured with orange zest and cinnamon.
- **Tarta de Santiago:** A moist almond cake dusted with icing sugar.

## Drinks

- **Sangria:** Red wine, orange slices, a splash of brandy and sparkling water, served over ice.
- **Fino sherry:** A dry, light sherry that pairs well with tapas.

# Korean Barbecue Night at Home

**Menu:** Three meats, six banchan, rice, lettuce wraps, and ssamjang. Everything here is sesame-free, and cilantro is left out.

## Meats and Marinades

**1. Bulgogi (thinly sliced ribeye or sirloin)**
- ½ cup soy sauce
- ¼ cup brown sugar
- ¼ cup grated Asian pear (or apple)
- 1 tbsp mirin
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tbsp neutral oil (avocado or canola)
- Black pepper, plus 2 scallions cut into 2-inch pieces

Slice the beef against the grain, about 1/8 inch thick (partially freezing it for 20 minutes makes this easier). Marinate 4 to 24 hours.

**2. Galbi (bone-in or boneless short ribs, butterflied)**
- ½ cup soy sauce
- ¼ cup sugar
- 3 tbsp mirin
- ¼ cup grated Asian pear
- 6 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp minced scallion
- 1 tbsp rice wine or dry sherry
- Black pepper

Marinate 6 to 12 hours. Grill over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side.

**3. Spicy pork (dwaeji bulgogi)**
- 2 tbsp gochujang
- 1 tbsp gochugaru (Korean chili flakes)
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1 tbsp mirin
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp grated ginger

Use thinly sliced pork shoulder and marinate 4 to 8 hours.

**4. Samgyeopsal (pork belly)**
No marinade needed. Grill plain slices and serve with salt, black pepper, and ssamjang.

## Banchan (Side Dishes)

**1. Kimchi**
Buy from your local Korean family shop. Serve it at room temperature or lightly grilled.

**2. Cucumber muchim (quick cucumber salad)**
- 2 Persian cucumbers, thinly sliced
- 1 tsp salt, then drain 10 minutes
- 1 tbsp gochugaru
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 clove garlic, minced

Toss everything together just before serving.

**3. Seasoned spinach (sigeumchi namul)**
- 1 lb spinach, blanched and squeezed dry
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 scallion, minced
- Pinch of salt
- 1 tsp neutral oil (in place of sesame oil)

**4. Soy-braised potatoes (gamja jorim)**
- 3 medium potatoes, cut into bite-size chunks
- ¼ cup soy sauce
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1 tbsp mirin
- 1 cup water
- Pan-fry the potatoes first for golden edges, then simmer with the sauce for 15 minutes until glossy.

**5. Korean egg roll (gyeran mari)**
Whisk 5 eggs with 1 tbsp milk, a pinch of salt, and 1 finely chopped scallion. Roll in a small nonstick pan in thin layers, then slice.

**6. Pickled radish (danmuji)**
Buy it pre-made from the Korean shop, or quick-pickle thin radish slices in equal parts rice vinegar and water with 1 tbsp sugar and a pinch of salt for 1 hour.

## Ssamjang (Dipping Sauce)
- 1 tbsp doenjang (soybean paste)
- 1 tbsp gochujang
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp water
- 1 scallion, minced

Stir together. Check the labels on your gochujang and doenjang, since some brands are processed on shared equipment with sesame.

## Serving Setup
- Steamed short-grain rice
- Butter lettuce or red leaf lettuce leaves for wraps
- Sliced garlic and green chilies for grilling
- Ssamjang and a small dish of salt and pepper for samgyeopsal

## Timeline
- **Two days before:** Buy kimchi, pickled radish, and gochugaru. Check all sauce labels for sesame.
- **Day before:** Marinate galbi and spicy pork. Pre-slice bulgogi beef and marinate it.
- **Morning of:** Make ssamjang, egg roll, spinach, and braised potatoes. Cook rice.
- **One hour before guests arrive:** Salt the cucumbers, then dress them just before serving. Set out banchan and lettuce.
- **At the table:** Grill meats on a tabletop grill or a cast-iron pan. Start with samgyeopsal and the sliced bulgogi, then add the galbi and spicy pork.

# Korean BBQ Night at Home

**Sesame-free note:** Sesame oil and sesame seeds appear in many traditional Korean dishes. Every recipe below is written without them. Check labels on store-bought gochujang, doenjang, ssamjang, and kimchi, since some brands contain sesame. Your family shop may be able to confirm which of their kimchi is sesame-free. Garnishes use green onion and perilla leaves, with no cilantro.

## Menu Overview
- **Meats:** Bulgogi (thin-sliced ribeye), LA-style galbi (short ribs), and spicy pork (dwaeji bulgogi)
- **Wraps:** Butter lettuce, perilla leaves, and steamed rice
- **Sauces:** Ssamjang and a sesame-free dipping sauce
- **Banchan:** 6 to 8 small side dishes
- **Drinks:** Barley tea, soju or Korean beer, and sparkling water

## Marinades (each serves about 4)

**1. Bulgogi (beef)**
- 1 lb thinly sliced ribeye (partially freeze for 20 minutes to slice easily)
- 1/3 cup soy sauce
- 1/4 cup grated Asian pear (or sweet apple)
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- 2 tbsp mirin
- 1 tbsp rice wine or cooking wine
- 5 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp grated ginger
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 3 green onions, cut into 2-inch pieces
- Marinate 2 to 12 hours. Skip sesame oil and add 1 tbsp neutral oil if you want some shine.

**2. LA Galbi (short ribs)**
- 2 lb flanken-cut short ribs
- 1/2 cup soy sauce
- 1/4 cup brown sugar
- 1/4 cup grated Asian pear
- 3 tbsp mirin
- 1 tbsp rice wine
- 6 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp black pepper
- Marinate 4 to 24 hours. Pat dry before grilling so the sugars caramelize without burning.

**3. Spicy Pork (dwaeji bulgogi)**
- 1 lb thinly sliced pork shoulder or belly
- 3 tbsp gochujang (check label for sesame)
- 1 tbsp gochugaru (Korean chili flakes)
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tbsp rice wine
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp grated ginger
- 1 small onion, sliced
- Marinate 2 to 8 hours.

## Banchan (Sesame-Free)

**1. Kimchi**
Serve from your family shop or a sesame-free brand. Cut into bite-size pieces.

**2. Oi Muchim (Spicy Cucumber Salad)**
- 2 Persian cucumbers, sliced thin
- 1 tsp salt, toss and rest 10 minutes, then drain
- 1 tbsp gochugaru, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sugar, 1 clove minced garlic, 1 green onion chopped
- Toss together. Serve chilled.

**3. Sigeumchi Namul (Garlic Spinach)**
- 1 lb spinach, blanched 30 seconds and squeezed dry
- 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 clove minced garlic, 1/2 tsp salt
- 1 tsp neutral oil (no sesame oil)
- Toss and season to taste.

**4. Kongnamul Muchim (Seasoned Bean Sprouts)**
- 8 oz bean sprouts, blanched 3 minutes and drained
- 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp rice vinegar, 1 clove minced garlic, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 green onion chopped

**5. Gamja Jorim (Soy-Braised Potatoes)**
- 1 lb baby potatoes, halved
- 1/3 cup soy sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 cup water, 1 tbsp mirin, 1 clove garlic
- Simmer 15 to 20 minutes until glossy and tender.

**6. Dubu Jorim (Braised Tofu)**
- 1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes and pan-fried until golden
- Simmer in 1/4 cup soy sauce, 2 tbsp water, 1 tsp sugar, 1 clove garlic, and 1 tsp gochugaru for 5 minutes.

**7. Gyeran Mari (Rolled Egg Omelet)**
- 4 eggs, beaten with 1 tbsp milk and a pinch of salt
- Roll thin layers in a nonstick pan and slice into rounds.

**8. Kkakdugi (Cubed Radish Kimchi)** *(optional)*
- Buy from a trusted source or make with daikon, gochugaru, fish sauce, garlic, and sugar.

## Ssamjang (Wrap Sauce)
- 2 tbsp doenjang
- 1 tbsp gochujang
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 tsp rice wine
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 green onion, minced
- 1 tsp water or as needed
Mix until smooth. Check labels on the doenjang and gochujang.

## Dipping Sauce
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 tsp gochugaru
- 1 tsp minced green onion

## Timeline
- **Two days before:** Buy short ribs, ask your family shop about kimchi, and start marinating the galbi.
- **Morning of:** Marinate the bulgogi and spicy pork. Make the oi muchim and ssamjang. Prepare the gamja jorim and dubu jorim.
- **1 hour before guests arrive:** Blanch and season the spinach and bean sprouts. Cut the gyeran mari. Set out the rice and lettuce.
- **During the meal:** Grill meats in batches on a grill pan, outdoor grill, or cast iron. Reheat the braised dishes as needed.

## Shopping List
- Ribeye, short ribs, pork shoulder or belly
- Asian pear, Persian cucumbers, spinach, bean sprouts, baby potatoes, firm tofu, daikon (if making kkakdugi)
- Butter lettuce, perilla leaves (kkaennip, often at Korean markets), green onions, garlic, ginger
- Soy sauce, mirin, rice wine, rice vinegar, brown sugar, sugar
- Gochujang, gochugaru, doenjang (sesame-free labels)
- Eggs, milk
- Short-grain rice
- Kimchi from your family shop

# Korean Barbecue Night at Home

This menu avoids sesame and keeps sodium low. Check labels on any packaged ingredients, since sesame and salt often appear in pre-made sauces and banchan.

## Banchan (Side Dishes)

1. **Kimchi:** Buy from your family-run Korean shop. Ask whether it contains sesame seeds, as some batches do.
2. **Cucumber muchim (smashed cucumber salad):** Sliced cucumber tossed with rice vinegar, a little sugar, minced garlic, gochugaru (Korean chilli flakes) and spring onion. It is sesame-free and needs no added salt.
3. **Pickled daikon (danmuji):** Yellow pickled radish from the Asian supermarket. It is sweet and crunchy and cuts through the richness of the meat. Rinse it briefly to reduce the sodium.
4. **Steamed egg (gyeran-jjim):** Beat two or three eggs with water in a ratio of about 1:1.5, add a pinch of salt or none, and steam gently until set. Top with spring onion.
5. **Braised potatoes with soy (gamja jorim), low-sodium version:** Cube potatoes and simmer in water with a splash of low-sodium soy sauce, a spoon of sugar and a little garlic until glazed.
6. **Blanched courgette or cucumber namul without sesame:** Lightly blanch courgette strips, squeeze dry and dress with a little garlic, a dash of rice vinegar and a few drops of neutral oil.

Skip the usual spinach and bean sprout namul, which typically use sesame oil and seeds.

## Marinades

**Bulgogi-style beef (sliced ribeye or sirloin, about 500g):**
- 2 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
- 1 grated Asian pear (or ½ grated apple) for natural sweetness and tenderising
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 3 cloves garlic, grated
- 1 tbsp rice wine or mirin
- 1 tsp grated ginger
- Freshly ground black pepper
- 1 tbsp neutral oil (not sesame)

Marinate for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.

**Gochujang chicken (thighs, about 500g):**
- 1 tbsp gochujang (check the label for sesame)
- 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
- 1 tbsp honey or sugar
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 2 cloves garlic, grated
- 1 tsp grated ginger
- A little neutral oil

Marinate for 2 to 4 hours.

**Pork belly (thin slices):** Cook it plain on the grill with just a little black pepper, then serve with the dipping sauces below.

## Dipping Sauces

- **Sesame-free ssamjang substitute:** Mix 1 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp doenjang (check the label), 1 tsp honey, 1 tsp rice vinegar and minced garlic and spring onion.
- **Simple dipping sauce:** Low-sodium soy sauce, rice vinegar, a pinch of sugar and sliced green chilli.

## Wraps and Fresh Elements

- Butter lettuce and perilla leaves (from the Asian supermarket; these are an excellent substitute for coriander in this setting)
- Sliced garlic and green chilli
- Steamed short-grain rice
- Thinly sliced spring onion

## Cooking Plan

1. **Two hours before:** Start the beef and chicken marinades. Make the cucumber muchim and pickle the daikon if not bought ready-made.
2. **One hour before:** Cook the steamed egg and braised potatoes, and make the ssamjang and dipping sauces.
3. **Just before guests arrive:** Set up a grill pan or outdoor barbecue, prepare the lettuce and rice, and arrange the banchan in small bowls.
4. **During the meal:** Grill the meats in batches and let everyone build their own wraps.

# Turkish Dessert Table for Eid

## Allergy Note
Many traditional Turkish sweets contain pistachios, walnuts, hazelnuts or almonds, so every item below has been chosen to be tree nut free. Buy from shops that label ingredients clearly, and check packaging for "may contain" warnings, since cross contamination is common in sweet shops that also sell nut-based products. Avoid baklava, künefe, ekmek kadayıfı, keşkül and most lokum unless you have confirmed the specific product is nut free. Aşure, the traditional "Noah's pudding," is also often made with hazelnuts and walnuts, so use the nut free version given below.

## Timeline by the Lunar Calendar
Eid dates depend on the sighting of the new moon, so confirm the exact date with your local mosque or community calendar before finalising plans.

- **About 10 days before 1 Shawwal (Eid al-Fitr):** Order any items from specialist shops, as they may need advance notice. Buy non perishable ingredients such as sugar, semolina and rosewater.
- **About 3 to 4 days before 1 Shawwal:** Bake the şekerpare and revani, which keep well in airtight tins.
- **1 Shawwal, morning:** Make the syrups for tulumba and lokma, and prepare the sütlaç so it can chill.
- **Eve of 1 Shawwal:** Fry the tulumba and lokma on the day, since they are best eaten fresh.

For Eid al-Adha (10 Dhu al-Hijjah), follow the same schedule, working back from that date.

## Shopping List
- Plain lokum, rose or lemon flavour, checked for nut free labelling
- Tahini helva (sesame based, naturally nut free)
- Fresh or dried figs, dates and apricots for garnish
- Pomegranate seeds and a small bowl of pomegranate molasses
- Rosewater and orange blossom water
- Full fat milk, cornflour, rice and vanilla for sütlaç and kazandibi
- Semolina, plain yoghurt, sugar and butter for revani and şekerpare
- Flour, yeast and vegetable oil for tulumba and lokma
- Cinnamon, sesame seeds and icing sugar for dusting

## Dessert Selection

**1. Sütlaç (Turkish Rice Pudding)**
Bake in small individual dishes and finish with a light cinnamon dusting. Serve chilled.

**2. Revani**
A semolina sponge soaked in lemon syrup, cut into diamonds and topped with a little dried fruit. Keeps well for several days.

**3. Şekerpare**
Small semolina cookies soaked in syrup, sold in many Turkish bakeries and easy to make at home. Use a plain version without almonds.

**4. Tulumba**
Crisp fried dough spirals soaked in lemon scented syrup. Best made on the day and served warm or at room temperature.

**5. Kazandibi**
A caramelised milk pudding with a burnt top, made from milk, sugar, cornflour and rice flour. Serve in small bowls.

**6. Tahini Helva**
Sliced and arranged on a platter with fresh figs or dates. Naturally nut free and a good option for guests who avoid dairy.

**7. Aşure (Nut Free Version)**
Traditional Noah's pudding made with wheat, dried beans, dried apricots, raisins, sugar and rosewater, omitting the hazelnuts and walnuts. Garnish with pomegranate seeds and cinnamon.

**8. Plain Lokum**
Rose or lemon flavoured Turkish delight, served in a dish with a dusting of icing sugar.

## Table Layout
- **Centre:** Aşure in a large serving dish, garnished with pomegranate seeds.
- **Left side:** Tulumba and lokma on a tiered stand.
- **Right side:** Sütlaç and kazandibi in individual bowls.
- **Front:** Revani and şekerpare on platters, with tahini helva and figs nearby.
- **Corners:** Lokum in small dishes, with a clear label for each item.

## Serving Tips
Label every dish clearly, marking the nut free items so guests can choose confidently. Provide small plates and spoons, and offer tea or Turkish coffee alongside the desserts, since both pair well with the sweet syrups.

Eid follows the Islamic lunar calendar, so the exact day depends on the sighting of the new moon. Eid al-Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal, the tenth month, and Eid al-Adha falls on 10 Dhu al-Hijjah, the final month. Confirm the date with your local mosque or community calendar once the moon has been sighted, then work backwards:

- **Seven to ten days before:** Buy shelf-stable items such as lokum and fresh fruit.
- **Three days before:** Bake revani and şekerpare, then store them in airtight tins.

**Nut-free desserts to bake**

- **Revani:** A semolina sponge soaked in lemon syrup. Leave off any almond or pistachio garnish.
- **Şekerpare:** Small semolina and butter biscuits soaked in syrup. Omit the traditional almond half on top.
- **Tulumba:** Fried choux-style dough fingers soaked in lemon-scented syrup.

- **Sütlaç:** Baked rice pudding with a caramelised top, sprinkled with cinnamon.
- **Kazandibi:** A milk pudding with a caramelised base, served cold.
- **Un helvası:** A flour and butter halva, toasted until golden and sweetened with sugar syrup. This is safer than tahini-based versions, which are sometimes made with pistachio.

**Nut-free desserts to buy**

- **Lokum (Turkish delight):** Choose rose, lemon or plain varieties. Pistachio, hazelnut and walnut versions are common, and bakery trays are often shared, so check the label and ask about cross-contamination before buying.
- **Fresh and dried fruit:** Figs, pomegranate, mandarins, grapes and dried apricots pair well with the sweets.
- **Turkish coffee and tea:** Serve çay in tulip glasses with sugar cubes.

**Desserts to avoid**

Several classic Turkish sweets contain tree nuts, so leave these off the table entirely:

- Baklava (usually pistachio, walnut or hazelnut)
- Künefe (usually pistachio)
- Aşure (often contains hazelnuts, walnuts or almonds)

# Turkish Eid Dessert Table: Nut-Free and Homemade

Eid al-Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal and Eid al-Adha on 10 Dhu al-Hijjah of the Islamic lunar calendar, so set your baking schedule by the moon sighting in your area. Plan to bake two or three days ahead, since most of these desserts keep well.

Because of the tree nut allergy, every recipe below is free of walnut, pistachio, almond, hazelnut and pine nut. Traditional baklava, künefe and ekmek kadayıfı are usually built around pistachio or walnut, so they are left off the list. Keep a clean, separate set of utensils for the nut-free items if anyone else in the household bakes with nuts.

## The Menu

**1. Sütlaç (Baked Rice Pudding)**
- Simmer 100 g short-grain pudding rice in 1 litre of whole milk with 80 g sugar and a vanilla pod until thick.
- Pour into small ramekins, dust with ground cinnamon, and bake at 200°C until the tops are golden.
- Serve warm or chilled.

**2. Revani (Semolina Cake in Syrup)**
- Beat 4 eggs with 200 g sugar, then fold in 200 g fine semolina, 100 g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 200 ml yoghurt and 100 ml vegetable oil.
- Bake in a greased tin at 180°C for about 30 minutes.
- Pour cold lemon syrup (sugar, water and a squeeze of lemon, boiled for 5 minutes) over the warm cake.

**3. Tulumba (Fried Syrup Dough)**
- Make a choux-style dough with butter, water, flour and a little egg.
- Pipe into short lengths, fry until golden, then soak in hot lemon-scented syrup for a few minutes.
- These are best eaten the same day.

**4. Kazandibi (Caramelised Milk Pudding)**
- Make a thick milk pudding with cornflour, sugar and milk, then pour it into a pan and let the base caramelise without stirring.
- Turn out and serve cut into squares, with the caramel side up.

**5. Homemade Lokum (Turkish Delight)**
- Dissolve 500 g sugar and 250 ml water, add 50 g cream of tartar, and simmer until 115°C.
- Stir in 100 g cornflour mixed with 250 ml water, then cook for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring until thick.
- Add rose water or lemon juice, pour into a lined tin, and leave overnight before cutting and dusting with icing sugar.
- Homemade lokum is safer for you than shop-bought, which often contains pistachio or hazelnut.

**6. Tahini Helva (Sesame Halva)**
- Melt sugar with water to a syrup, then stir in tahini and a pinch of salt until it thickens into a dense mass.
- Press into a tin and chill, then cut into slices.

**7. Fresh Fruit**
- Include figs, pomegranate seeds, grapes, and sliced oranges with a light orange blossom water syrup. These balance the richer sweets.

## Table Layout

- **Back row:** tall items such as the tulumba platter and the revani squares.
- **Middle row:** the kazandibi and sütlaç in serving dishes.
- **Front row:** lokum and tahini helva on small plates, with the fresh fruit scattered between them.
- Label every dish clearly with its name and the words "nut-free", so guests with allergies can choose safely.

## Timeline

- **Three days before:** make the lokum and tahini helva, and store them in airtight tins.
- **Two days before:** bake the revani and make its syrup.
- **Day before:** prepare the sütlaç and kazandibi, then chill them.
- **Morning of:** fry the tulumba and soak it in syrup, then arrange the table and add the fruit.

# Turkish Eid Dessert Table

Eid dates follow the Islamic lunar calendar. Eid al-Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal, and Eid al-Adha on 10 Dhu al-Hijjah. Moon sighting can shift the date by a day, so plan your baking around the local announcement. Everything below is made at home and contains no tree nuts.

## Menu

**1. Revani (semolina cake in syrup)**
A moist, fragrant cake soaked in lemon syrup. Make it one day ahead, because it improves overnight.
- 1 cup semolina, 1 cup plain flour, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup yoghurt, 3 eggs, 100 g melted butter, 1 tsp baking powder, zest of 1 lemon, 1 tsp vanilla
- Bake at 180°C for 35 to 40 minutes in a greased tin.
- Syrup: 2 cups sugar, 2 cups water, juice of 1 lemon. Simmer 10 minutes, then pour over the warm cake.

**2. Tulumba (crispy fried syrup dough)**
Best made the same day or the morning before, and reheated gently if needed.
- Choux-style dough from 1 cup water, 2 tbsp butter, 1 cup flour, 2 eggs, and a pinch of salt.
- Pipe into thin strips, fry in hot sunflower oil until golden, then soak in cold lemon syrup for a few minutes.

**3. Sütlaç (baked rice pudding)**
A classic Turkish dessert with a caramelised top. Make it the day before so it can chill properly.
- 1 litre milk, 100 g short-grain rice, 100 g sugar, 1 tbsp cornflour, 1 tsp vanilla.
- Cook the rice in milk until soft, stir in sugar and cornflour, and pour into individual dishes. Grill briefly until the tops are spotted brown.

**4. Kazandibi (caramelised milk pudding)**
A dessert with a burnt-sugar base, which gives it its name. Make it the day before.
- 1 litre milk, 6 tbsp cornflour, 150 g sugar, 2 tbsp butter, 1 tsp vanilla, 1 tsp mastic (optional).
- Cook the milk mixture until thick, pour into a greased tray, chill, then sprinkle sugar over the top and caramelise it with a blowtorch or under a hot grill.

**5. Şekerpare (semolina sugar cookies)**
Make these two or three days ahead, since they keep well in an airtight tin.
- 1 cup semolina, 1 cup flour, 150 g butter, 1/2 cup icing sugar, 1 egg yolk, 1 tsp baking powder.
- Shape into small rounds, bake at 170°C for about 20 minutes, then soak briefly in cold syrup. Omit the almond halves usually placed on top.

**6. Homemade Lokum (Turkish delight)**
Plain or rose-flavoured versions are safest. Avoid any recipe that calls for pistachio or hazelnut, and check that any flavourings or decorations are nut-free.
- Dissolve 2 cups sugar in 2 cups water with 1 tbsp lemon juice. Add 1/2 cup cornflour mixed with 1 cup water, and cook, stirring constantly, for about 30 minutes until thick.
- Flavour with rose water or lemon, pour into a lined tin, and leave to set for at least 12 hours. Dust with icing sugar.

**7. Tahini Helva**
Sesame-based, so it is nut-free, and it keeps well for several days.
- Cook 1 cup semolina in 4 tbsp butter until golden, then stir in 1 cup sugar dissolved in 1 cup water, and 1/2 cup tahini.
- Press into a lined dish and cool before serving.

## Timeline

- **Three days before:** Make the şekerpare and helva, and prepare the lokum.
- **Two days before:** Bake the revani and soak it in syrup. Make the kazandibi and sütlaç.
- **The day before:** Chill the sütlaç and caramelise the kazandibi just before serving. Cut the revani.
- **On the day:** Fry the tulumba in the morning, soak it in syrup, and arrange the table.

## Serving Tips

- Set out small glasses of unsweetened Turkish tea or Turkish coffee alongside the sweets.
- Label every dish clearly with its ingredients, so guests with allergies can choose safely.
- Use separate serving spoons for each dessert to avoid cross-contact.

# Eid Turkish Dessert Table

This plan uses only nut-free sweets. Turkish desserts often contain pistachio, walnut or almond, so the list avoids baklava, künefe and many traditional lokum (Turkish delight) and şekerpare, which are common nut carriers.

## Timing by the Lunar Calendar

Eid dates follow the Islamic lunar calendar, so confirm the exact day with your local moon sighting or mosque announcement.

- **Eid al-Fitr (1 Shawwal):** Make the milk puddings and syrups 2 days before. Fry the lokma and tulumba on the morning of the celebration so they stay crisp.
- **Eid al-Adha (10 Dhu al-Hijjah):** Bake the revani and helva 1 to 2 days ahead, since both keep well. Prepare the kazandibi the day before.

## The Menu

**Bake at home**

1. **Sütlaç (Turkish rice pudding):** Simmer short-grain rice in milk with sugar, then pour into small cups and grill the tops lightly until golden. Serve chilled.
2. **Revani (semolina cake in syrup):** Use semolina, flour, eggs, yoghurt and butter, then soak in a lemon-scented syrup. Omit the almond halves traditionally placed on top, and use a nut-free baking tray and utensils if you are sharing a kitchen with nut products.
3. **Kazandibi (caramelised milk pudding):** Cook milk, sugar, rice flour and starch until thick, then caramelise the base in the pan. This is naturally nut-free.
4. **Tulumba (syrup-soaked fried dough):** Pipe choux-style dough into hot oil, fry until golden, then soak in cold syrup with a little lemon. Serve warm or at room temperature.
5. **Tahini helva (sesame halva):** Make it with plain tahini and sugar, checking that no pistachio flavouring is added. Sesame is not a tree nut.

**Buy from a trusted nut-free source**

6. **Lokma:** Some fried dough bakeries make these without nuts. Ask about fryer oil and surfaces, since shared equipment can cause contamination.
7. **Plain Turkish delight (rose, lemon or plain flavour):** Check that the label says "nut-free" or shows no tree nut ingredients, as many varieties contain pistachio or hazelnut. Buy sealed packs where possible.

**Avoid entirely**

- Baklava (usually walnut or pistachio)
- Künefe (usually pistachio)
- Almond or pistachio versions of şekerpare and lokum

## Serving Suggestions

Arrange the chilled puddings in small glass cups on one side of the table, the cakes and fried sweets on tiered stands in the centre, and the helva and Turkish delight in small dishes at the end. Label every dish clearly with its ingredients, and keep the nut-free items physically separate from any nut-containing sweets you might also serve for other guests.

# Singaporean Hawker-Style Dinner at Home

This menu is shellfish-free and cilantro-free. Read ingredient labels carefully, since shellfish shows up in less obvious places.

## Hainanese Chicken Rice (rice dish)
**Chicken:** Poach one whole chicken (about 1.5 kg) in water with smashed ginger, scallion whites, and a pinch of salt. Once cooked, plunge it into ice water, then chill and slice.

**Fragrant rice:** Rinse 2 cups jasmine rice. Fry it briefly in 2 tbsp chicken fat or neutral oil with minced garlic and ginger. Cook it in the reserved poaching stock, adding 2 pandan leaves (knotted) and a little salt.

**Chili-ginger sauce:** Blend 3 red chilies, a thumb of ginger, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp lime juice, 1 tsp sugar, and a pinch of salt. Serve it with a little sesame oil.

**Serve with:** Sliced cucumber, a drizzle of dark soy sauce, and scallion garnish.

## Char Kway Teow (noodle dish)
This version skips the prawns and cockles, and the shrimp paste.

- 400 g flat rice noodles (kway teow), loosened in warm water
- 150 g chicken thigh, thinly sliced
- 2 Chinese sausages (lap cheong), sliced (check the label for shellfish)
- 2 eggs, beaten
- 1 cup bean sprouts
- Garlic-chili paste (no shrimp paste)
- Sauce mix: 1 tbsp dark soy, 1 tbsp light soy, 1 tsp sweet soy or sugar, 1 tsp oyster-free sauce (see note below)

**Method:** Get a very hot wok. Fry the chicken and sausage until nearly cooked. Push them aside, scramble the eggs, then add the garlic-chili paste. Add the noodles and sauce mix and toss over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until charred at the edges. Fold in the bean sprouts and scallion greens and serve immediately.

**Note:** Standard char kway teow uses oyster sauce, which is a mollusk product. Skip it and use the soy-based mix above, or use a mushroom-based vegetarian oyster sauce if you check the label carefully.

## Achar (side)
Quick-pickled vegetables: combine julienned cucumber, carrot, and cabbage with a brine of rice vinegar, sugar, salt, and a pinch of turmeric. Chill for at least an hour.

## Dessert: Chendol
- Pandan-green rice flour jelly (or store-bought pandan jelly)
- Coconut milk, lightly salted
- Gula melaka (palm sugar) syrup, warmed
- Shaved or crushed ice
- Optional: red beans or sweet corn

Layer the jelly over ice, add the coconut milk and palm sugar syrup, and serve.

## Shopping Tip
Pandan leaves and fresh herbs are usually available at Asian supermarkets, where you can also find the kway teow noodles and gula melaka. Ask the staff or check labels if you're unsure whether a sauce or sausage contains shrimp or oyster products.

# Singaporean Hawker-Style Dinner at Home

This menu pairs Hainanese chicken rice with wonton noodles and a fresh cucumber side. I have kept it low in sodium and free of shellfish, including shrimp paste and dried shrimp, which are common in Singaporean cooking.

## 1. Hainanese Chicken Rice (Main Rice Dish)

**Chicken:**
- 1 whole free-range chicken, about 1.5 kg, with skin removed
- 1 thumb-sized piece of ginger, sliced
- 4 spring onions, tied in a knot
- 2 litres water
- Unsalted chicken stock, if you have it, for extra flavour

Bring the water, ginger and spring onions to a gentle boil. Lower the chicken in, return to a simmer, cover and poach for about 25 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it rest in the liquid for 15 minutes. Lift it out, plunge it into iced water, then drain and cut into pieces.

**Rice:**
- 300 g jasmine rice, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon sesame oil
- 2 garlic cloves, crushed
- 1 thumb-sized piece of ginger, bruised
- 350 ml of the reserved poaching broth, skimmed of fat

Fry the garlic and ginger in the sesame oil until fragrant, add the rinsed rice and stir for a minute. Add the broth, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on low for about 15 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes before fluffing.

**Ginger-scallion sauce:**
- 3 tablespoons finely chopped ginger
- 2 spring onions, finely sliced
- 2 tablespoons hot oil (heated until it sizzles when poured over the ginger)
- 1 teaspoon low-sodium soy sauce
- A squeeze of lime

Mix everything together just before serving.

## 2. Wonton Noodles with Char Siew-Style Chicken (Noodle Dish)

**Noodles and toppings:**
- 200 g fresh egg noodles, cooked and drained
- 150 g chicken thigh, marinated for at least 2 hours in 1 tablespoon low-sodium soy sauce, 1 teaspoon honey, 1 teaspoon hoisin (check the label for sodium), 1 crushed garlic clove and a pinch of five-spice, then roasted at 200°C for about 20 minutes
- 4 chicken or pork-free wontons, filled with minced chicken, ginger and spring onion, and simmered until cooked
- 1 handful of bok choy, blanched

**Broth:**
- 800 ml unsalted chicken stock
- 1 slice of ginger
- 1 teaspoon sesame oil
- A few drops of white pepper

Simmer the stock with the ginger for 10 minutes, then remove the ginger and stir in the sesame oil and pepper. Place the noodles, wontons, sliced chicken and bok choy in bowls and pour the hot broth over them.

## 3. Cucumber Salad (Side)

- 1 cucumber, sliced thinly
- 1 teaspoon rice vinegar
- 1 teaspoon sugar
- A pinch of chilli flakes
- A handful of fresh mint and Thai basil, both from the Asian supermarket

Toss everything together and chill for 10 minutes before serving.

## Tips for Low Sodium Cooking

- Use unsalted stock and low-sodium soy sauce throughout.
- Taste before adding any salt. The ginger, spring onion and sesame oil provide plenty of flavour.
- Check labels on hoisin, chilli sauce and any pre-made wonton wrappers, as they are often high in sodium.
- Avoid store-bought achar and sambal unless you can confirm they contain no shrimp paste or dried shrimp.

Here's a hawker-style dinner with three dishes: Hainanese chicken rice, chicken laksa, and mee goreng. I've left out shellfish and coriander, and noted where common recipes call for them.

## 1. Hainanese Chicken Rice (with rice and chilli sauces)

**Chicken and rice**
- 1 whole chicken (about 1.5 kg), or bone-in thighs
- 2 tbsp salt, 1 tsp sesame oil
- 5 slices ginger, 4 garlic cloves, 2 pandan leaves (tied in a knot)
- 300 g jasmine rice, rinsed
- Chicken stock to replace the poaching water, plus 1 tbsp chicken fat or oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced, for the rice

**Method**
1. Rub the chicken with salt and sesame oil. Simmer the whole bird in water with the ginger, garlic, and pandan for about 35 to 40 minutes, until cooked through.
2. Plunge the chicken into ice water for a few minutes to firm the skin, then drain and rub with sesame oil.
3. Fry the rinsed rice briefly in chicken fat with minced garlic. Add the reserved stock (about 1.5 times the rice volume) and cook as you would plain rice.
4. Serve sliced chicken on the rice with cucumber slices.

**Chilli and ginger sauces**
- Chilli: blend 4 red chillies, 1 garlic clove, 1 tbsp ginger, 1 tbsp lime juice, a pinch of sugar, and salt.
- Ginger: grate 2 tbsp ginger and mix with 2 tbsp hot oil from the chicken pot (or neutral oil), plus a pinch of salt.

## 2. Chicken Laksa

**Ingredients**
- 2 tbsp laksa paste (check the label: many contain dried shrimp or belacan, so buy a shrimp-free brand or make your own)
- 400 ml coconut milk, 500 ml chicken stock
- 300 g chicken thigh, sliced
- 200 g thick rice noodles (or yellow noodles)
- 100 g bean sprouts, 1 handful of fried tofu puffs, halved
- 2 tbsp sambal chilli (check for shrimp paste)
- Thai basil or mint for garnish instead of coriander

**Method**
1. Fry the laksa paste in a little oil until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
2. Add the stock and simmer, then stir in the coconut milk and the chicken. Cook until the chicken is done, about 10 minutes.
3. Blanch the noodles and bean sprouts, then divide them among bowls.
4. Ladle the broth over, then add tofu puffs, sambal, and herbs.

## 3. Mee Goreng Mamak (Fried Yellow Noodles)

Traditional versions often use prawns, and some use oyster sauce, so this version swaps those out.

**Ingredients**
- 250 g yellow noodles, blanched and drained
- 150 g chicken thigh, thinly sliced
- 1 potato, cut into small cubes and fried until golden
- 2 eggs, 100 g firm tofu, cubed
- 3 tbsp sweet dark soy sauce, 1 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp chilli paste
- 2 tbsp mushroom sauce (in place of oyster sauce)
- 2 garlic cloves, 2 shallots, minced
- 1 handful of bean sprouts, sliced spring onion

**Method**
1. Stir-fry the garlic and shallots in oil until fragrant.
2. Add the chicken and cook through, then add the tofu and potato.
3. Push everything to one side, scramble the eggs, then mix them in.
4. Add the noodles, soy, ketchup, chilli paste, and mushroom sauce. Toss on high heat for 3 to 4 minutes.
5. Finish with bean sprouts and spring onion.

## Serving Tips
- Serve the chicken rice with the chilli and ginger sauces and some cucumber.
- Add a bowl of lime and chilli for the laksa.
- Pandan and lemongrass from the Asian supermarket can add a lot of flavour to the rice and laksa.

# Singaporean Hawker-Style Dinner at Home

This menu has three dishes: a rice dish, a stir-fried noodle dish, and a noodle soup. All are free of shellfish and coriander, and they are adjusted for a low-sodium diet.

## 1. Hainanese Chicken Rice (rice)
- **Chicken:** Poach a whole chicken in unsalted water or stock with smashed ginger, spring onion, and a few peppercorns. Chill it in iced water to keep the skin silky.
- **Rice:** Fry jasmine rice briefly with garlic and ginger, then cook it in the poaching stock with a pandan leaf. Use unsalted stock to keep the sodium down.
- **Sauces:** Make a ginger-spring onion sauce with fresh ginger, spring onion, a little oil, and a pinch of salt. Make a chilli-garlic sauce with red chilli, garlic, lime juice, and a small amount of sodium-reduced soy sauce.
- **Serve:** Slice the chicken and arrange it over the rice with cucumber slices. Dip sparingly in the sauces.

## 2. Chicken and Tofu Char Kway Teow (noodles)
- **Noodles:** Use flat rice noodles, soaked until pliable and drained well.
- **Stir-fry:** Heat a wok until very hot. Fry diced chicken thigh, firm tofu, and garlic. Add the noodles with a little sodium-reduced dark soy sauce for colour, and a small amount of kecap manis for sweetness.
- **Add-ins:** Add beansprouts, chives, and beaten egg. Scramble the egg into the noodles.
- **Tip:** Traditional versions use prawns, cockles, and oyster sauce. Leave these out, as they contain shellfish. Use Chinese chives in place of any shellfish garnish.

## 3. Chicken Laksa (noodle soup)
- **Broth:** Blend shallots, garlic, ginger, lemongrass, dried chillies, turmeric, and toasted coriander seeds into a paste. Fry the paste until fragrant, then add unsalted chicken stock and light coconut milk.
- **Noodles:** Serve with thick rice vermicelli or yellow noodles, blanched briefly.
- **Toppings:** Add shredded poached chicken, fried tofu puffs, beansprouts, halved boiled eggs, and laksa leaves. Use fresh mint or Thai basil in place of coriander.
- **Note:** Do not add belacan (shrimp paste) or dried shrimp, which are common in laksa but contain shellfish.

## Low-Sodium Tips
- Use unsalted stock in all three dishes.
- Replace standard soy sauce with a sodium-reduced version.
- Use fish sauce sparingly, as it is high in sodium.
- Season with lime juice, chilli, and fresh herbs for flavour in place of salt.

## Shopping Notes
- Look for laksa leaves, pandan leaves, and kecap manis at an Asian supermarket. Fresh herbs there are often cheaper and fresher.
- Check labels on pre-made pastes and sauces for shrimp, prawn, or oyster extracts.

# Singaporean Hawker-Style Dinner at Home

This menu pairs Hainanese chicken rice with chicken mee goreng, plus a simple vegetable side. It is adapted for a low-sodium diet and is free of shellfish.

**Shellfish check:** Many hawker sauces contain shellfish, including oyster sauce, shrimp paste, dried shrimp, and prawn stock. The recipes below avoid these, but check the labels of every packaged ingredient, especially stock cubes and sauces.

## 1. Hainanese Chicken Rice (Main Rice Dish)

**Chicken and rice**
- 1 whole chicken, about 1.5 kg, or 4 bone-in thighs
- 1 thumb-sized piece of ginger, sliced
- 2 spring onions, tied in a knot
- 2 litres of water
- 1 litre of low-sodium chicken stock
- 300 g jasmine rice, rinsed
- 1 tbsp chicken fat or neutral oil, plus 1 smashed garlic clove for the rice

**Ginger-chilli sauce**
- 3 cm fresh ginger, finely grated
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 2 red chillies, finely chopped
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp sugar
- 2 tbsp hot chicken broth from the pot

**Method**
1. Bring the water, ginger, and spring onions to a boil in a large pot. Lower the chicken into the water, reduce the heat to a gentle simmer, and cook for about 35 minutes until the internal temperature reaches 74°C.
2. Lift the chicken into iced water for 5 minutes, then drain and chop it into pieces.
3. Fry the rinsed rice in the oil with the smashed garlic for 2 minutes. Add 450 ml of the reserved broth mixed with the low-sodium stock, then cook covered over low heat for about 18 minutes.
4. Mix the sauce ingredients together. Serve the chicken on the rice with sliced cucumber and the ginger-chilli sauce.

## 2. Chicken Mee Goreng (Noodle Dish)

This is a Mamak-style fried noodle with no prawns or cockles.

**Ingredients**
- 200 g yellow egg noodles, such as mee
- 150 g boneless chicken thigh, thinly sliced
- 100 g firm tofu, cubed
- 2 eggs, beaten
- 1 handful of bean sprouts
- 2 spring onions, cut into lengths
- 1 small onion, sliced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp chilli paste, such as sambal oelek
- 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 tbsp tomato purée
- 1 tbsp neutral oil
- Fresh coriander leaves, to garnish, if you enjoy them
- 1 lime, cut into wedges

**Method**
1. Soak the noodles in hot water for 5 minutes until softened, then drain.
2. Fry the tofu in a hot wok until golden, then set aside.
3. Stir-fry the chicken in the oil for 4 minutes until cooked through. Add the onion and garlic and cook for 2 minutes.
4. Stir in the sambal, tomato purée, low-sodium soy sauce, and sugar. Add the noodles and toss over high heat for 2 minutes.
5. Push the noodles to one side, scramble the eggs in the space, then mix everything together. Add the tofu, bean sprouts, and spring onions.
6. Serve hot with lime wedges.

## 3. Garlic Kailan (Vegetable Side)

- 200 g kailan or broccolini
- 2 garlic cloves, sliced
- 1 tsp neutral oil
- 1 tsp low-sodium soy sauce
- A squeeze of lime juice

Blanch the kailan for 1 minute, then drain. Fry the garlic in the oil until fragrant, add the greens, and toss with the soy sauce and lime juice for 1 minute.

## 4. Dessert: Light Chendol

- Shaved ice
- Pandan jelly, made from a packaged mix
- Coconut milk, unsweetened or light
- A drizzle of palm sugar syrup

Layer the ingredients in a glass and serve chilled.

## Sodium-Saving Tips
- Choose low-sodium stock and soy sauce, and use half the sambal if it is salty.
- Season with lime, ginger, and chilli to keep flavour high without extra salt.
- Use fresh herbs from the Asian supermarket where possible, as they add flavour with minimal sodium.

Traditional fondue relies on Gruyère and Vacherin, and your dairy allergy rules those out, so the plan below keeps the communal, social character of the original with ingredients that contain no milk products. Check every packaged item, since milk ingredients often hide in bread, crackers, stock, mayonnaise and chocolate.

## Starter: Dairy-Free "Cheese" Fondue

**Ingredients:**
- 1 cup raw cashews, soaked in hot water for 30 minutes and drained
- 1 cup dry white wine or unsalted vegetable stock
- 2 tbsp nutritional yeast
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 2 cloves garlic
- 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 1 tbsp kirsch (optional, traditional)
- Salt and a pinch of nutmeg

**Method:** Blend the cashews, wine or stock, nutritional yeast, lemon juice, garlic and mustard until completely smooth. Pour into a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the cornflour slurry, and whisk until the mixture thickens into a glossy sauce, which takes about five minutes. Stir in the kirsch and season. Transfer to a fondue pot and keep warm over a low flame. If anyone has a nut allergy, replace the cashews with cooked, puréed white beans or cauliflower.

**Dippers:**
- Crusty sourdough or baguette cubes (check the label for milk)
- Boiled baby potatoes
- Steamed broccoli and cauliflower florets
- Apple and pear wedges
- Cherry tomatoes
- Cornichons (small pickled gherkins)
- Sautéed mushrooms

## Main: Fondue Bourguignonne

This meat course contains no dairy, so it works well as the centrepiece of the evening.

**Ingredients:**
- 800g beef sirloin or fillet, cut into 2cm cubes
- 1 litre neutral oil, such as sunflower or rapeseed, heated to about 180°C in the fondue pot

**Sauces:**
- Garlic aioli made with eggs, oil and lemon (confirm that the mayonnaise base is dairy-free)
- Chimichurri, made with flat-leaf parsley, garlic, red wine vinegar, oregano and olive oil
- Tomato ketchup mixed with horseradish and Worcestershire sauce (check the label)
- Dijon mustard with a little honey

Spear the beef on fondue forks and cook each piece for 30 to 90 seconds, depending on how you like it done. Keep the oil at a steady temperature, and never let water come near it. Use a thermometer and avoid overfilling the pot.

## Dessert: Dark Chocolate Fondue

**Ingredients:**
- 200g dark chocolate, confirmed dairy-free (many brands contain milk, so read every label)
- 200ml full-fat coconut cream
- 1 tbsp kirsch or pear brandy
- A pinch of sea salt

**Method:** Heat the coconut cream gently in a saucepan until it just begins to simmer. Remove from the heat, add the chopped chocolate and stir until melted and smooth. Stir in the spirit and salt, then transfer to a fondue pot on low heat.

**Dippers:**
- Strawberries
- Orange segments
- Pineapple chunks
- Grapes
- Marshmallows (confirm they are dairy-free)
- Dairy-free shortbread or biscuits

## Timing and Tips

Start with the cheese-style starter about 30 minutes before guests arrive, so it is ready and warm when they sit down. Cook the beef in batches once everyone has gathered, then clear the pot and prepare the chocolate while people finish their main. Keep a small bowl of fresh water and a lid nearby in case of a fire, and never leave the burner unattended. Label every dish clearly so that guests with allergies can see at a glance what is safe to eat.
